package: MYOPIA: Understanding the Limits of Tree-Based Reasoning in Vision-Language Models -- reproducibility archive

supports_paper_claim.claim: The supplementary material reports complete T=0, tree-with-history, 10-prompt zero-shot, global-label, numbered-choice, and run-to-run results, along with full tree-audit specifications and node counts.

mapping.10-prompt zero-shot: S4 (Table S3, Figure S1); underlying RunId 0-9 rows in data/dbs/
mapping.run-to-run results: S4-S5 (Table S4); RunId rows in data/dbs/

contents.src/: Evaluation harness (main.py, run_all_experiments.py, prompt_library.py, config.json, models/, datasets/, results/initiate_db.py), generator-evaluator tree pipeline (tree_generation/), and the analysis scripts that regenerate every table and figure (evaluation/).
contents.data/dbs/: The four result databases, uncompressed SQLite: gtsrb, mnist, cifar10, mscoco. Each holds a single `answers` table keyed on (Image_path, LLM_name, Include_memory, Include_description, Include_zero_shot_label, temperature, RunId). Stage them into src/results/ before running any analysis script; there is no separate merge step. gtsrb.db takes GPT-4o's primary-condition rows from the path-logged re-run of that condition and every other row from the original pass, so each row comes from exactly one run -- see the GTSRB entry under Known caveats in README.md.
contents.data/: Derived CSVs, byte-for-byte the output of the analysis scripts on the shipped databases: agreement/, baselines/, bootstrap_ci_holm.csv, constrained_choice_probe/, cot_baseline/, global_list_probe/, grounding/, image_grounded_verification/, inference_cost/, label_conditioned_verification/, tree_error_analysis/, tree_quality_audit/.
contents.trees/: Human-readable dumps of the four evaluated decision trees (128 internal nodes and 153 leaves in total: GTSRB 22/43, MNIST 8/10, CIFAR-10 9/10, MSCOCO 89/90) plus the CUB-200 demo tree (18 internal, 20 leaves), which demonstrates the generation pipeline and is not evaluated. The evaluated trees are defined in src/tree_generation/*_tree.py; the demo tree also ships as JSON at src/tree_generation/automated_tree_generation/cub200_demo_tree.json.
contents.prompts/: Every prompt the harness sends, loaded through src/prompt_library.py: templates.json (12 named templates), ten zero-shot paraphrases and per-class descriptions per dataset, the image-description prompt, the CHiLS superclass captions, the zero-shot prompt generator, and the tree generator/evaluator prompt sets.
contents.sample_ids/: Fixed evaluation subsets: 901 GTSRB, 1000 MNIST, 1000 CIFAR-10, 850 single-category MSCOCO image identifiers.
contents.tables/: LaTeX of the reported tables, byte-for-byte the output of the analysis scripts: tab_zs_vs_tree_extended, tab_agreement, tab_grounding, tab_gtsrb_depth, tab_inference_cost, tab_supp_full.

excluded: the paper and supplementary text (LaTeX sources and PDFs) and their hand-made figures
API credentials, .env files, and local environment configuration
raw provider responses and request caches
the datasets themselves; only sample identifier lists and derived label metadata are included

license.datasets: Not covered by the MIT grant. Dataset access remains governed by the original licenses and terms (GTSRB, MNIST, CIFAR-10, MSCOCO), as described in Section 9 of the main paper and in src/README.md.

reproducibility.offline_tier: Every table and figure reported in the main paper regenerates from data/ with no API access; see the README.md reproduction matrix for the commands and the ordering constraint (oracle_extraction_analysis.py before cost_frontier.py). Supplement Tables S1, S2 and S8-S9 regenerate the same way; the data behind the remaining supplement tables ships in data/.
reproducibility.deduplication: All analysis queries read rows through src/evaluation/db_utils.py's ANSWERS view, which drops the legacy Data/GTSRB/all_sequences_training/ duplicates; skipping it inflates GTSRB denominators from 901 to up to 915.
reproducibility.accuracy_convention: Correct when int(Class) == int(prediction_class); the denominator is every row of the condition, so unparseable answers and images with no logged traversal count as wrong (supplement S1).
reproducibility.coverage_rule: The main-paper table reports a cell only where its condition covers at least 90% of a full dataset pass (paper_table.py --min-coverage); tables/tab_supp_full.tex reports every condition with its n.
reproducibility.python: 3.9+; analysis re-verified on 3.12. Dependencies in src/requirements.txt (CLIP baselines additionally need torch/transformers).
reproducibility.limits: Model responses are obtained from hosted APIs and are not bit-reproducible even at T=0; see supplement S10.
